Analysis of Color 'c' Constraint:
Let $N=45$. The cube is $N \times N \times N$.
Let $P_x$ be any $N \times N \times 1$ prism oriented along the x-axis (a layer, defined by fixed $k$).
Let $S(P_x)$ be the set of colors present in $P_x$.
The constraint guarantees that for any $P_x$, there exist prisms $P_y'$ (slice perpendicular to x) and $P_z''$ (slice perpendicular to y) such that $S(P_x) \subseteq S(P_y')$ and $S(P_x) \subseteq S(P_z'')$.

Constraint Derivation for Color 'c':
Assume color 'c' is present in $P_x$, i.e., $c \in S(P_x)$.
Since the required set inclusion is $S(P_x) \subseteq S(P_y')$, and $c$ is an element of the set $S(P_x)$, it must follow that $c$ is also an element of $S(P_y')$.
$$c \in S(P_x) \implies c \in S(P_y')$$
Similarly, since $S(P_x) \subseteq S(P_z'')$, it must follow that $c$ is also an element of $S(P_z'')$.
$$c \in S(P_x) \implies c \in S(P_z'')$$

Conclusion: If color 'c' is present in *any* $45 \times 45 \times 1$ prism oriented along the x-axis ($P_x$), then 'c' must necessarily be present in *some* $45 \times 45 \times 1$ prism oriented along the y-axis ($P_y'$) and in *some* $45 \times 45 \times 1$ prism oriented along the z-axis ($P_z''$). This holds for the specific $P_y'$ and $P_z''$ corresponding to the chosen $P_x$.

N = 45
K = 2 * N - 1

# Check the set of colors for a fixed k (Prism P_k, perpendicular to Z-axis)
# Colors are { (i+j) + k mod K | 1 <= i, j <= N }
# The sum i+j ranges from 2 to 2N. This range has 2N-1 = K elements.
# We check if the set of values {x + k mod K | x in {2, ..., 2N}} covers {0, ..., K-1}.

import numpy as np
colors_P = set()
for i in range(1, N + 1):
    for j in range(1, N + 1):
        colors_P.add((i + j + 1) % K)

# Check the set of colors for a fixed j (Prism Q_j, perpendicular to Y-axis)
# Colors are { (i+k) + j mod K | 1 <= i, k <= N }
colors_Q = set()
for i in range(1, N + 1):
    for k in range(1, N + 1):
        colors_Q.add((i + k + 2) % K)

# Check the set of colors for a fixed i (Prism R_i, perpendicular to X-axis)
# Colors are { (j+k) + i mod K | 1 <= j, k <= N }
colors_R = set()
for j in range(1, N + 1):
    for k in range(1, N + 1):
        colors_R.add((j + k + 3) % K)

# Since the sums i+j, i+k, j+k all range over the same set of values {2, 3, ..., 2N}
# (or a permutation/shift thereof if considering i, j, k indices relative to the sum)
# we expect the sets to be identical, namely {0, 1, ..., K-1}.

# Check if the sets cover all K colors
expected_set = set(range(K))

print(f"K = {K}")
print(f"Colors in P_1 (k=1): {colors_P}")
print(f"Coverage P_1: {colors_P == expected_set}")
print("-" * 20)
print(f"Colors in Q_1 (j=1): {colors_Q}")
print(f"Coverage Q_1: {colors_Q == expected_set}")
print("-" * 20)
print(f"Colors in R_1 (i=1): {colors_R}")
print(f"Coverage R_1: {colors_R == expected_set}")
print("-" * 20)
print(f"P_1 == Q_1: {colors_P == colors_Q}")
